howToUse: This script bank gives you the exact sentences to use in three conversations that tend to surface the moment you commit to a programme like this — before your niche is finalised. You don't need to read it all at once: go straight to whichever script matches the conversation you're facing today and use the words as written. The goal is to keep you moving rather than stalled in a holding pattern that feels like preparation.
promise: Use these scripts word-for-word and you will get through the three conversations that most commonly send women back into research mode — without needing a polished niche to do it. You stay in motion, and the programme does its job.

    "name": "Script 1: What to Say to Yourself When the Doubt Surfaces",
    "type": "script",
    "instructions": "Read this aloud or write it in your notes app the moment you catch yourself thinking 'I should wait until I'm clearer on my niche.' Use it as a full replacement for the loop, not a supplement to it.",
    "content": "## The Internal Re-Direct Script

**When to use it:** The moment the thought appears — *I'm not ready to commit, I still don't know my niche* — and you feel the pull back toward the notes app, another podcast, another worksheet.

---

### Say this (out loud or in writing):

> *"Waiting until my niche is clear is the exact reason it won't become clear. I cannot think my way to a niche I haven't tested. The programme is the process — I don't need the answer before I do the work."*

---

### Then ask yourself these two grounding questions:

**Question 1:**
> *"What, specifically, am I waiting to know before I move forward?"*

Write the answer in one sentence. If the answer is a version of *"which niche is right,"* say:

> *"That is the question the programme is built to answer. I cannot answer it ahead of schedule."*

**Question 2:**
> *"What is one thing I can do in the next 20 minutes that is inside the programme, not outside it?"*

Write the answer. Do that thing.

---

### The pattern this interrupts:

The holding pattern looks like research. It feels like diligence. What it actually is: using the absence of a finished niche as permission to delay the work that produces the niche. The Career Layer Excavation Process inside your programme is built specifically to work through your actual career history — not a generic worksheet — so the niche emerges from what you've already done, not from what you can figure out alone in a notes app. The doubt is real. Acting on it is optional.

---

### Pocket version (save this as a phone note):

> *"I don't need the answer to start the work. The work produces the answer. I move now."*"

  {
    "name": "Script 2: What to Say to a Partner or Spouse Who Asks 'Are You Sure Yet?'",
    "type": "script",
    "instructions": "Use this word-for-word the next time your partner asks whether you've figured out your niche, whether this is the right time, or whether you're sure — before you have a tidy answer to give them.",
    "content": "## The Partner Conversation Script

**When to use it:** When your spouse or partner asks some version of *"Do you know what you're doing yet?"* or *"Have you settled on what your business is going to be?"* and you feel the pressure to either have a finished answer or to hedge and back away from the commitment you've made.

---

### Opening (choose the version that fits your dynamic):

**Version A — matter-of-fact:**
> *"Not yet, and that's actually on purpose. The programme I've joined starts with a structured process to identify exactly that — it's called [Career Layer Excavation] and it works through my actual career history rather than asking me to guess. I'm in the early part of the process right now."*

**Version B — if they seem worried about money or time:**
> *"I know it looks like I don't have it nailed down yet, and I want to explain why that's okay at this stage. The programme is specifically designed for women who don't have a finished niche when they start — that's the point of the first phase. What I do have is a structured process and a coach working through it with me. I'm not guessing; I'm inside a method."*

**Version C — if they've asked this more than once:**
> *"I know you've asked before and I've said 'not quite yet' each time. Here's what's actually happening: identifying the right niche for a consulting business takes a specific kind of structured excavation — you can't just decide it. I'm doing that work inside the programme right now. What would be most helpful is for you to know that I'm on track, not that I have a finished answer today."*

---

### If they push — *"But what would you even do for clients?"*

> *"The short version is [describe your pre-family professional background in one sentence — e.g., 'I spent 12 years in HR managing organisational change for mid-size companies']. The programme is helping me identify which part of that expertise is the one people will pay a consulting fee for, rather than assume is just background knowledge. That distinction matters and it's exactly what we're working through."*

---

### The closing line (use this to end the conversation clearly):

> *"I'm not stuck. I'm inside a process. The answer will be specific and I'll have it — I'd rather have the right one than a fast one."*

---

### What not to say:

- ❌ *"I'm still figuring it out"* — sounds indefinite, invites more doubt
- ❌ *"I'm not sure yet"* — accurate but gives the conversation nowhere to go
- ❌ A long explanation of the programme features — they need confidence, not a brochure"
  },
  {
    "name": "Script 3: What to Say in Your First Network Conversation When You Don't Have a Polished Answer",
    "type": "script",
    "instructions": "Use this the next time someone from your professional past — a former colleague, a LinkedIn connection, an industry contact — asks what you're working on now. Copy the core lines directly; swap in your own career background where marked.",
    "content": "## The Network Conversation Script

**When to use it:** Any professional conversation — in person, on a call, via LinkedIn message — where someone asks *"What are you doing these days?"* or *"Are you back in [industry]?"* and you don't yet have a niche statement clean enough to recite.

---

### The core answer (use this when the question is casual):

> *"I've just started working with a coach to build a consulting practice — the focus is going to be in [your broad professional area, e.g., 'operations,' 'talent and culture,' 'financial services compliance,' 'healthcare management']. I'm in the early phase of narrowing down the specific offer, but the direction is clear. Honestly, the most useful thing right now is reconnecting with people like you who are still inside the industry — you've got context I've been away from."*

---

### Why this works:

It names a direction without requiring a finished niche. It signals you're in a structured process, not drifting. And it immediately turns the conversation toward them — which is exactly where early network conversations should go, because what they tell you about the industry's current problems is raw material for your niche, not a distraction from it.

---

### If they ask a follow-up — *"What kind of consulting?"*

> *"Still getting specific — intentionally. I spent [X years] in [role/sector], most of it focused on [1–2 sentence description of your core expertise, e.g., 'building out performance frameworks for mid-market professional services firms']. I'm working out which part of that is the sharpest problem to solve for clients, rather than rushing to an answer that's too broad. Can I ask — what are the problems inside [industry/sector] right now that feel like no one's quite solving them well?"*

---

### If they offer to introduce you to someone:

> *"I'd love that — even at this stage. The conversations I'm most interested in right now are with people inside [industry/sector] who are dealing with [the broad area your expertise covers]. That's genuinely helpful for where I am in the process, and I promise I won't pitch anyone — I'm in listening mode for the next few weeks."*

---

### LinkedIn version (for a message reply when someone asks what you're up to):

> *"Great to hear from you — yes, I'm back. I've started building a consulting practice in [broad professional area] and I'm in the early structured phase of getting specific on the offer. Still the best part of this process, honestly — talking to people like you who are close to where the real problems are. Would love to catch up properly if you have 20 minutes in the next few weeks."*

---

### The one sentence to memorise:

> *"I'm in the early phase of getting specific — the direction is [your broad area] and I'm talking to people inside the industry right now, which is exactly where I want to be."*"

    "instructions": "Run this 60-second check before each conversation to calibrate which script to pull and how much to say — it takes you from 'I don't know what to tell people' to 'I know exactly how much to share right now.'",
    "content": "## 60-Second Niche-Readiness Check

**Use before:** any conversation where your niche or business direction might come up — with yourself, a partner, a network contact, or anyone else.

---

### Step 1 — What do I actually have right now? (tick what's true today)

- [ ] I know my broad professional background (the industry and rough role I held)
- [ ] I have a sense of the general area I want to work in, even if it's not precise
- [ ] I have a structured process underway to get specific (the programme)
- [ ] I do NOT yet have a named, finished niche
- [ ] I do NOT yet have a packaged offer
- [ ] I do NOT yet have paying clients

**Tally:** How many of the first three did you tick? That's how much substance you have to draw on. One or more: enough to have any of the three conversations in this script bank.

---

### Step 2 — Which conversation am I about to have?

| Situation | Script to use |
|---|---|
| Doubt surfacing internally, urge to research instead of act | Script 1: The Internal Re-Direct |
| Partner / spouse asking if you're sure yet | Script 2: The Partner Conversation |
| Professional contact asking what you're doing now | Script 3: The Network Conversation |
| You're not sure which applies | Start with Script 1 — the others follow from there |

---

### Step 3 — What is the one thing I will NOT do in this conversation?

Choose one and hold it:

- [ ] I will not say *"I'm still figuring it out"* with no follow-up sentence
- [ ] I will not over-explain the programme
- [ ] I will not pretend to have a finished niche I don't have
- [ ] I will not let the conversation end without a clear next step (for network conversations: a follow-up call, an introduction, or a specific question answered)

---

### After the conversation — one-line debrief:

> *"What did I learn from this conversation that is useful material for my niche?"*

Write one sentence. This is not journaling — it's intelligence-gathering. Every conversation at this stage gives you data. The Career Layer Excavation Process in your programme will use this."

nextStep.body: These scripts are designed to hold you in motion until your niche work inside the programme produces the specific answer. The Career Layer Excavation Process — your first structured phase — is where that answer gets built from your actual career history, not from your notes app. Open your programme portal, go to Phase 1, and begin the excavation session. Bring to it any notes from the network conversations you've already had — what people said, what problems they named, what assumptions they made about your background. That material is not background noise. It's input.
